The
Global AI
Index

The first index to benchmark nations on their investment, innovation and implementation of artificial intelligence

By Joe White, Serena Cesareo, Hannah Schuller

Making sense of artificial intelligence on a global scale

In the past year, AI capabilities have rapidly advanced across fields ranging from coding to higher mathematics. Industry valuations and capital expenditure have soared to hundreds of billions of dollars, and nations are racing to build their own “sovereign” compute capacity.

Sceptics warn of an AI bubble, but governments increasingly fear missing out on what could be the most fundamental general-purpose technology since electricity.

Pillars

The Global AI Index is composed of 108 indicators, collected from 24 different public and private data sources. These are split across three pillars and seven sub-pillars.

Implementation

“Talent” focuses on the availability of skilled practitioners in artificial intelligence solutions, from top AI research scientists working on the cutting edge of AI to developers and professionals applying AI at a practical level.

“Infrastructure” assesses the physical and material foundations of AI, including high-performance computing, semiconductor production and electricity capacity.

“Operating environment” focuses on public attitudes towards, and adoption of, AI at a broad societal level.

Innovation

“Research” is the ability to generate novel scientific knowledge in AI, measured through the scale and quality of AI research publications, innovations and breakthroughs in AI model techniques and architectures, and the strength of educational institutions.

“Development” is the ability to apply AI scientific knowledge and create new AI assets and products at a practical level, measured through open-source AI activity and adoption, and the volume of AI-related patents.

Investment

“Government strategy” gauges the depth of national government commitment to artificial intelligence, including planned investments and spending in training, research, infrastructure and private sector support.

“Commercial ecosystem” focuses on the scale and breadth of private investment into AI companies and the dynamism of the commercial ecosystem.
